questions.title: Which best describes your current role and how you originate residential loans?
questions.prompt: This assessment is for producing residential Loan Originators. Choose all that fit—retail/direct lender, mortgage broker, bank LO, producing team leader; mostly self-generated, company-generated, or blended. If your role is primarily processing, underwriting, operations, secondary markets, or non-producing leadership, this version is not designed for that role.

questions.title: What is the main business result you want over the next 12 months?
questions.prompt: For example: funded loans, funded volume, personal/owner business income, or another measurable production result. Include the target and whether it applies to you, your team, or another scope.

questions.title: What did you fund in the last 12 months, and what have you funded in the last 90 days?
questions.prompt: Use loans your business counts as closed/funded. Enter funded units and volume if you know both. If your company defines “funded” differently, tell us which completed event you use.

questions.title: How much of your business is Purchase, Refinance, or another residential loan purpose?
questions.prompt: Use the same 12-month funded baseline when possible. Choose Not applicable for paths you do not originate; that is different from zero or unknown.

questions.title: Which business or professional sources consistently create mortgage opportunities for you?
questions.prompt: Your Opportunity Source Network includes relationships or channels such as Realtor partners, builders, financial professionals, other professional referrals, company/branch opportunities, direct/digital channels, or self-generated activity. A contact is not automatically an opportunity. For each meaningful source, use aggregate numbers only.

questions.title: How is your past and current customer network contributing to repeat, Refinance, and referral business?
questions.prompt: Your Customer Relationship Network means past/current borrowers or customers whose continuing relationship can create a repeat purchase, Refinance, or friends/family referral. Use aggregate counts only—no borrower names or loan files.

questions.title: Walk us through your opportunity-to-funded pipeline for the last 12 months, and the last 90 days if available.
questions.prompt: An Opportunity is a person or household with a plausible current mortgage need—not every contact or database record. Enter only stages you actually track. Purchase and Refinance paths appear separately when applicable.

questions.title: What do you consistently do to build and maintain the relationships that create business?
questions.prompt: Separate your Opportunity Source Network from your Customer Relationship Network. A CRM is a tool, not a system. For each real system, tell us who it serves, what happens, how often, how it is delivered, who owns it, and how you know it is working.

questions.title: Who handles the major parts of your business today, and what work is limiting your capacity?
questions.prompt: Consider relationship work, application/preapproval, file coordination, processing/underwriting follow-up, closing, and customer follow-up. Identify owners, handoffs, sustainable load, and any service or quality effect. Do not assume a processor is the answer.

questions.title: What company, platform, product, process, or policy limits materially affect your results?
questions.prompt: For example: product/program fit, pricing, underwriting or operations turn times, technology, lead distribution, geographic reach, or company policy. Choose “none known” if that is your actual answer.

questions.title: What do you believe matters most right now—what is holding the business back, or, if you are on track, what should you protect or build on?
questions.prompt: Tell us what makes you think that. “Nothing material” and “I’m not sure” are valid answers.

questions.title: What commitments or operating priorities are you accountable for right now, and how consistently are they happening?
questions.prompt: For each material priority, include the owner, expected cadence or target, actual execution/results, and what you have learned. This is about execution evidence, not moral judgment.

questions.title: Your numbers show a material drop or delay at [purpose/stage]. What is happening there?
questions.prompt: For example: customer drop-off, incomplete applications, qualification/preapproval, property search, process/approval delays, lock/funding fallout, or cycle-time issues. “Unknown” is valid.

questions.title: To evaluate your income or economics goal, what are the minimum business numbers we should use?
questions.prompt: Use only what applies—for example compensation/revenue per funded loan, relevant variable cost per loan, fixed business cost, and whether the goal is individual, team, branch, or salary-based. Do not include personal household finances.

questions.title: These answers do not line up: [claim A] and [claim B]. Which is correct, or are they measuring different things?
questions.prompt: We will make one clarification attempt. If you are not sure, say so—we will preserve the uncertainty rather than average or choose for you.
